subject: OEM distribution rights & brand guardrails for LumenEdge integration
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@lumenedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OEM distribution rights & brand guardrails for LumenEdge integration

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the demo last week. LumenEdge's use case (bundling our runtime inside your appliance and offering a managed plan to end customers) sounds like a good fit. Attached is a short-draft we use internally to frame distribution and branding options (OEM-Terms-Draft-v1.pdf).

High-level asks from our side to get the conversation going: 
- Confirm the intended redistributable surface: full runtime binary + quantized weights, or just an API gateway to Redwood-hosted endpoints?
- Expected install footprint and offline/air-gapped needs (KMS or HSM integration?).
- Co-branding model: full white-label, co-branded, or private-label? We usually map three levels with different marketing/usage rights.
- Support & SLA expectations for bundled customers (who is the first responder?).

Can you share the list of legal and procurement contacts we should loop in? If it helps, we can schedule a 30-min call next week to walk through three distribution options and what each would require (tech, legal, pricing).

Attaching draft, happy to iterate.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: OEM-Terms-Draft-v1.pdf (pdf, 42 KB)

From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@lumenedge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Ross <anna.ross@lumenedge.com>, Brian Lowe <brian@lumenedge.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: OEM distribution rights & brand guardrails for LumenEdge integration

Jordan —

Thanks for sending this over and for the call. Quick answers and context from our side: 
- Redistribution: we plan to ship a pre-configured image that includes the runtime + model artifacts (quantized) to our channel partners. We also want an option for on-prem customers to run locally in isolated networks.
- Security: KMS integration will be required (we use HashiCorp Vault primarily). For air-gapped customers we may need a signed binary and offline activation mechanism.
- Branding: target is a private-label option for enterprise customers; co-branding for certain reseller offers.
- Support: LumenEdge will be first-line support; for escalations to Redwood we expect an agreed RTO/RPO and an escalation path.

I've attached an internal reqs spreadsheet that outlines expected licensing seats, deployment patterns, and some initial volume estimates. Anna and Brian are cc'ed — Anna will take lead on the redlines from a legal perspective.

Can you confirm whether Redwood allows distribution of the compiled runtime and model weights under a commercial OEM license (we'd need redistribution rights and a mechanism for revocation if needed)? If not, what alternatives do you suggest (e.g., runtime-only, signed bundles, or hosted routing)?

Best,
Sam
Product Partnerships Manager
LumenEdge

Attachment: Lumenedge-OEM-Reqs.xlsx (spreadsheet, 38 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@lumenedge.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OEM distribution rights & brand guardrails for LumenEdge integration

Sam —

Thanks for the quick context. I'll lay out the technical distribution options so legal and product can map to them: 

Option A — Hosted-backend + SDK: LumenEdge packages a lightweight SDK and proxies requests to Redwood-hosted inference. Pros: we retain model assets, easier to enforce revocation and telemetry. Cons: requires reliable connectivity and increases per-token cost.

Option B — Signed runtime + quantized model bundle (redistributable): Redwood signs runtime builds and provides encrypted model blobs. We can support per-instance activation tied to a customer ID and periodic token checks (for offline customers we can allow quarterly re-auth). Pros: low latency, offline capability. Cons: more complex to support and requires clearly defined revocation and update processes.

Option C — Container image with limited-weight selection: We provide a curated, smaller-weight model variant for redistribution with stricter usage limits and no telemetry. Pros: easier compliance for regulated customers. Cons: lower model quality for some tasks.

Operational asks (from infra/ops): 
- Activation/License key service (we can provide a lightweight licensing endpoint).
- Telemetry: for RBC (billing and quality), we request anonymous usage metrics. For enterprise/regulatory customers, we can disable telemetry per contract.
- Security: support for customer-managed KMS + signed artifacts.

I've attached a short note that maps implementation complexity vs. risk (distribution-options.md). Happy to join a technical call next week to run through the integration checklist and SSO/KMS flow.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Engineering — Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: distribution-options.md (markdown, 6 KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OEM distribution rights & brand guardrails for LumenEdge integration

Sam —

Appreciate the details. From GTM & brand perspective, a couple quick notes: 
- For private-label enterprise customers we typically request a simple acknowledgement: Redwood retains ownership of the model and trademarks, LumenEdge may rebrand the UI/assets for those customers under the OEM agreement.
- Co-marketing: for co-branded offers we'd like to define joint case study rules and logo usage (I'll send our standard co-marketing addendum).
- Reseller pricing: please send proposed volumes/tiers in the spreadsheet so we can map to a resale discount.

Jordan/Karthik — can you confirm product/legal guardrails needed before we share marketing materials with channel partners? I want to avoid channel partners offering the runtime as "our own model" without the proper support/updates.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference

From: Anna Ross <anna.ross@lumenedge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: OEM distribution rights & brand guardrails for LumenEdge integration

Jordan/Karthik/Vanessa —

Attaching our initial redlines (Lumenedge-redlines.docx). High level items we expect to negotiate: redistribution rights, revocation/patching obligations, indemnities for third-party content, telemetry & data handling, and a clear SLA for security patches. We also have a few procurement checks (insurance, audit rights, and export controls).

A few specific asks up front: 
- Can Redwood provide a revocation mechanism and a documented patch cadence for distributed bundles?
- Is there a default export-control classification for the runtime + model (we need to know whether any OFAC/EAR licenses apply)?
- For telemetry, we need an opt-in/opt-out process per customer and a definition of anonymized metrics.

If you can provide answers to these three items, we can prepare a prioritized redline list and a timeline for procurement. We can also arrange a legal-only sync if that helps.

Best,
Anna Ross
Senior Counsel
LumenEdge

Attachment: Lumenedge-redlines.docx (docx, 55 KB)
